Very bad experience. Had paid advance of Rs.5000/- for 7 day trip to Gujarat for 6 adult and 1 kid. Due to undue circumstances, the kid had to be admitted to hospital for getting high fever and the trip had to be cancelled informing well in advance before the trip schedule. Konkan tourist was so harsh that he refunded Rs.3000/-only and deducted Rs.2000/- for cancelling the trip for circumstances beyond our control. Doesn't consider humanitarian ground for cancellation.

In response to the owner of Konkan tourist, it is still unfair to deduct 40% of the advance for cancelling the trip for the circumstances beyond our control even after informing well in advance the situation of sickness of the kid. Telephonically it was informed to deduct Rs.1500/- and thereafter Konkan tourist deducted Rs.2000/- which is quite unfair.
Secondly, amount deducted beyond the amount of Rs.1500/- is for no services offered.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
We truly empathize with the situation — emergencies can happen unexpectedly, and we’re hoping the child is recovering well. That said, this is precisely why an advance payment is collected, as it secures bookings and confirms arrangements made in good faith. It’s always interesting how “advance” is sometimes assumed to mean “fully refundable,” even when vehicles and drivers have been blocked for an entire 7-day trip during the busy Diwali season.

While our policy and mutual understanding state that advances are non-refundable, we still chose to refund ₹3,000 purely on humanitarian grounds — not because we were obligated to, but because we wanted to be considerate. The remaining ₹2,000 went toward the driver who had reserved those dates exclusively for this trip.

We’re sorry our gesture of goodwill is being viewed otherwise, but we genuinely wish your family good health and hope to serve you under happier circumstances in the future.
